reason: 5.32.0 extends the containment verdict from the file system to Postgres on Neon: a shell act that targets a database (psql, pg_restore, prisma, drizzle-kit) can run against an ephemeral Neon branch of the target, the operator reviews the statement, the schema diff and the output once on /approvals, and Promote raises a single-use act-hash-bound grant that replays the original statement on production (dashclaw contained apply). Server: db_branch eligibility, per-basis capability negotiation (allow_contained:db), dashclaw/contained-db-<seg> refs, db promote mints the ORIGINAL act at the original risk score, reversible:false; the evidence classifier now grades database shell commands (database flag, inline SQL via classifySql). Hooks: dashclaw_db_containment.py (Neon client, target detection, rewrite, credential scrub), one branch per session bound to one endpoint, inline connection-string commands never advertised. Zero new API routes, pages, MCP tools, SDK methods, CLI commands or policy types (surface budget untouched); no migration. Both SDKs unchanged and republished at 5.32.0 by the tag. @dashclaw/cli 0.13.0 (contained diff/apply learn db refs). Plugin bundle 3.2.0 (new hook module). @dashclaw/mcp-server stays at 3.1.5.
